# Water Capital Wire

> A free daily read on the business of water for managers, investors and operators: capital, companies, technology, infrastructure and water security, with every fact sourced and dated. Each edition has a lead story traced through the water cycle (source, treatment, use, reuse, discharge), briefs across the water economy, weekly spotlights on a company, a leader, a supplier, an innovation and an investor, a capital desk of deals and firms, a water atlas on stress, demand, infrastructure, emerging sectors and security, a watchlist of water equities, a project calculator and an events calendar. General information, not investment advice.

## Today's edition
- [Federal money for Colorado River water conservation fell by more than 70%, a new report finds](https://watercapitalwire.com/): November 27, 2026. Federal spending on Colorado River Basin water conservation fell from $675 million to $200 million across five programs in 18 months, a new report finds, as basin states still lack a deal on post-2026 rules.
- [Capital: WaterSense raises €5.75 million in pre-seed money and grants for sensor-based river monitoring](https://watercapitalwire.com/#money)
- [Reuse: The world added 21.1 million m³ a day of water reuse capacity in 2025, led by record additions in China](https://watercapitalwire.com/#world)
- [Utilities: Thames Water is in the High Court today asking to put its debt extension to creditors](https://watercapitalwire.com/#thames)
- [Technology: Texas lawmakers file data center bills, two aimed at water use, ahead of the 2027 session](https://watercapitalwire.com/#texas)
